title: Three-minute inference demo: scripts + safeguards (draft)
content:
Slide 1 — Goal and timing
- Objective: show value of Redwood inference in ~3 minutes for an engineering/PM audience.
- Focus: predictable latency, fallback behavior, and cost control hooks.
- Timing: 15s intro, 90s live demo, 30s failover scenario, 45s wrap + next steps.

Speaker note: start by setting expectation: "I’ll demo a simple customer flow and what happens if we hit capacity or latency spikes."

---

Slide 2 — Setup (1 line for audience)
- Environment: Hosted API (us-west) with reserved fallback to Dedicated model variant.
- Input: user prompt -> chat-style assistant -> structured JSON output.
- Observable SLOs: p50 latency, per-token cost estimate.

Speaker note: call out that the demo uses the same API your engineers will call; show the single curl/SDK line on the slide.

---

Slide 3 — Demo script: happy path (60–75s)
- Show code snippet (curl or JS SDK) sending prompt and function call.
- Play: receive streaming tokens, show latency metric in Console, and final structured JSON (entities + score).
- Key lines to speak: "Streaming keeps the UI responsive, cost per request is visible in the Console, and the model returned structured entities we can parse directly."

Short code snippet to flash (speaker reads):
- Node: client.responses.create({model: 'rw-1-1', input: 'Extract names and dates from the text', stream: true})

---

Slide 4 — Quick talking points (30s)
- Why this matters to eng teams: deterministic tail-latency, prefix caching, and straightforward SDK.
- Data point: typical p95 for similar demos ~120–220ms (regional), cost per 1k tokens shown.
- One-liner for execs: "Predictable inference economics without owning the infra."

Speaker note: Have the Console open to the latency/cost chart to reinforce the numbers.

---

Slide 5 — Failure mode: latency spike (demonstration, 30–45s)
- Simulate: throttle or region outage -> auto-fallback kicks to cheaper model variant in another region.
- Show what the SDK returns: fast failover response with explanation header and degraded-but-usable output.
- Scripted remark: "You’ll notice we still return an answer and include a quality-indicator header — apps can act on that."

Seller cue: if customer asks about data residency, say: "Fallback respects policy — routing only where permitted; Dedicated/private options remove cross-region fallbacks."

---

Slide 6 — Failure mode: noisy or unsafe output (20–30s)
- Trigger: adversarial prompt -> Redwood Optimize policy detects regression in quality.
- Demonstrate: guardrail layer replaced generation with a rerank/filtered output and logs an eval alert.
- Scripted remark: "We keep a quality signal tied to prompt sets so teams can detect regressions early and rollback models."

Operational note: show the rollout/rollback toggle in Console; emphasize audit logs.

---

Slide 7 — Quick troubleshooting checklist for SEs (bullets)
- If streaming stalls: check KV cache hits and suffix length, fallback to smaller sequence length model.
- If p95 spikes: confirm routing policy, check Dedicated pool saturation, consider transient autoscale.
- If output quality drops: check recent model rollouts, prompt-set regressions, and Optimize alerts.

One-liner to hand the customer: "We treat inference like a service with observability and predictable mitigations — not a black box."

---

Slide 8 — Callouts + next steps (closing)
- Quick ask: follow-up pilot with sample dataset (we’ll measure latency, cost, quality on your traffic).
- Materials to leave: short runbook, demo recording link, sample contract stub (Reserved capacity options).
- Ask: schedule a 45-minute technical workshop that runs the pilot.

Speaker close: "If you’re interested, we can get a pilot running in days, and we’ll instrument the metrics you care about."

---

Appendix / Seller play snippets (copypasta)
- "If they worry about buffer bloat: explain continuous batching and how we cap latency using per-customer pools."
- "If they ask about price volatility: point to Optimize recommendations and quantization options that reduce cost while keeping quality."
- "If they want absolute data residency: note Private deployments with VPC & on-prem available; we can run the same Console without cross-region fallback."

Notes to self (TODOs)
- Add a short animated gif showing streaming tokens + Console metric overlay.
- Add a slide with 'one-sentence legal/procurement cues' for SAs.
- Run through with Marco & Priya, collect timing feedback.

End of draft
